back: The degree of the numerator is less than the degree of the denominator. Only proper fractions split directly into partial fractions.

front: Partial-fraction form for distinct linear factors
Partial-fraction form for a repeated linear factor
back: $\dfrac{px^{2} + qx + r}{(ax + b)(cx + d)^{2}} \equiv \dfrac{A}{ax + b} + \dfrac{B}{cx + d} + \dfrac{C}{(cx + d)^{2}}$

front: Partial-fraction form with an irreducible quadratic factor
back: $\dfrac{px^{2} + qx + r}{(ax + b)(cx^{2} + d)} \equiv \dfrac{A}{ax + b} + \dfrac{Bx + C}{cx^{2} + d}$

front: How do you find the constants?
back: Multiply through by the denominator to get an identity; substitute the roots of the factors; equate coefficients for any constant left; check at another value.

front: What do you do with an improper fraction?
back: Divide first: polynomial + proper fraction, then split the proper fraction.

front: Which board examines partial fractions of improper fractions?
back: ZIMSEC (Form 5). Cambridge 9709 (Paper 3 only) uses proper fractions only.
Each simple fraction is easy to integrate (giving logarithms), to expand as a binomial series, or to sum by the method of differences.
